participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, running the meeting)
summary: Standing team meeting: wins, per-rep projections, setter KPIs, then a closer-only review of Andrew Musial's best call of the week — a $6,000 close with a 39-year-old psychiatrist. Andrew had a five-close week including a hat trick; Ben Byrne had a thin week and said he would not hit four. Kyla Louie admitted she had stopped dialling after her no-show list and was given a hard KPI of 120 dials or four sets. The call review is the substantive part: Chris praised Andrew's discovery as textbook while correcting three things — sharing personal stories too early in discovery, using financing interest as a lever to push a prospect toward paying up front, and failing to open-wallet a prospect who asked about monthly payments. Chris also stated the company's real targeting, which does not match the ICP as it is described to prospects on live calls. The recording ends mid-sentence when Chris removes the note-taking bots to have a private conversation with Ben.
notable: Chris stated the actual target market in terms that directly contradict the ICP quoted to prospects on live calls: 'We're targeting people, essentially, who have like, their entire life put together, except fitness. Like guys in their 40s, 50s ... they might have some injuries, they might have some things, and they need help to actually, like, get their health in order. Like, they need to lose maybe 20, 30, 40 pounds. That's the sweet spot.' The stated ICP says the opposite — 'it's not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight'. A new VSL is being built around the revised target.

The $4,000 three-month tier is a real, manager-known product, not a rep improvisation. Andrew's week included 'the 4K split in two', and a prospect named Tamer 'got in for three months, but he will do the six months ... he will only top up with the 2K, that is secured' — i.e. $4,000 now plus $2,000 later to reach the six-month programme.
Payment-plan pricing was stated on the reviewed call: a prospect asking for $1,000/month was told 'it's not going to be 1k per month. It's going to be 1,200', i.e. $7,200 against a $6,000 programme.

Chris explicitly corrected the use of interest as a closing lever: 'you went right into telling him what it would be and using the interest against him to want to pay more, so you use interest as the thing as to why he should do it, which I don't really love that frame.' This is a useful counterweight to how financing was presented on Ben Byrne's own calls this week.

Open-wallet is framed as maximising extraction: 'Once you figure out exactly what they can do, you can offer ... Because that's how you collect the most cash out from somebody that you can collect', followed by 'maybe you find out he could have piffed. And he has $20,000 on a credit card, and then you find out, dude, just put it on the credit card.'

The reviewed prospect disclosed an undiagnosed back injury from deadlifting — 'I think I pulled my back, so that put me out for a little bit. So, I never got diagnosed' — and was closed at $6,000 without any clinician clearance being sought. Chris's verdict on the call was 'It's like a textbook, great process, great prospect.'
Two prospects were characterised by ethnicity and name during the review: 'he's also half Indian, I think. So work for them is always a priority' and 'He's got the whitest name ever, though.'

Chris coached Ben specifically to be more confrontational after Ben reported a friend told him he was 'too nice' on calls: 'have conversations that are really like polarizing with people ... Just say what needs to be said and then pick up the pieces afterwards.' Read against Ben's two sales calls this week, where he conceded price rather than held it, this is the live coaching thread.

Andrew shares his personal WhatsApp number with prospects at the end of calls. Chris did not object — 'I don't see an issue with that' — but redirected the framing so the prospect understands Trevor is the coach: 'your coach is going to be Trevor ... At that, I always emphasize that you're going to be working with Trevor only.'

Setter operations: Kim Forbes-Sobers is dialling roughly 10:30am to 6:30pm Eastern with good volume but poor connect rates and four DQs out of six contacts in a day; Kyla Louie admitted 'I just haven't done it. It's a bad excuse. I haven't put in the volume' and was set a KPI of 120 dials or four sets.

A DQ'd prospect who was sent free resources instead of being sold came back warm two days later — 'two days into kettlebells, really fun ... then maybe I'll see about working with Trevor' — the second week running that the free-resource nurture has produced a re-engagement.

Useful coaching worth preserving: Chris's 'false positives' point, that reps attribute closes to specific lines and then bloat their calls with them, when what actually closes is presence and certainty — 'It's never, it's not usually the words you say.'
Recording ends abruptly at 47:29 when Chris says 'Let me get rid of these note takers. Just wanna have a heart to heart with you.' Whatever was said to Ben next is not in the corpus.
